Subject: FW: sudden p99 latency spikes across our hosted endpoints (internal)

Internal: summary and ask — please treat as exec-level escalation if confirmed root cause maps to GPU memory fragmentation/OOM behavior.

What we have so far:
- Customer: Alpine AI (US). Affected time window: 15:07–15:22Z.
- Symptoms: p95/p99 regressions + intermittent 5xx; customer saw throughput drops. Token sizes ~75.
- Initial platform signals: correlated increase in OOM retries and slab/reserve churn on a subset of GPU hosts in us-west-2 pool; autoscaler attempted container restarts in a narrow cluster segment.

Immediate asks:
1) Rishi / Hannah: confirm whether we saw KV cache eviction storms or allocator slab fragmentation that would explain retries. Attach any trimmed logs and quick root cause hypothesis in a reply.
2) Marissa / Grace: prepare a short exec note for Alpine (and internal execs) summarizing impact, ETA for mitigation, and any credits/sla remediation options.

I'll keep the customer updated and propose a mitigation (route to a compatible model variant or temporary capacity pin).

—Jordan
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T16:12:18Z
Subject: Re: FW: sudden p99 latency spikes across our hosted endpoints (internal)

Quick technical read: attached short log snippets (oom_log_snippets.txt). Observations:
- Multiple host-level OOM signals during the window; memory allocator logged high fragmentation and repeated small-block failures leading to fallback allocations and NVMe spill for cache.
- Continuous batching and large KV cache entries (due to a traffic pattern with many mid-length prompts) caused unexpected slab compaction pressure on the allocator.
- Autoscaler restarts reduced immediate throughput but did not prevent tail latency until skewed hosts were drained and requests re-routed.

Recommendation (short-term): 1) Route Alpine traffic to a healthy host pool (pin to dedicated capacity) or fall back to a quantized model variant with lower KV footprint. 2) Apply emergency allocator config to reduce fragmentation (lower slab size / enable compacting GC) — ops risk noted.

I've added the snippets and a short repro trace to the incident record. Will follow up with more logs.

—Rishi

Date: 2027-07-01T23:42:10Z
Subject: Update & next steps — mitigation applied, mutual action plan attached

Elena / Tom — update from our side and next steps. Apologies again for the incident. TL;DR: we identified host-level allocator fragmentation and repeated small-block OOMs in a subset of the us-west-2 serving pool that correlated with your p99 spikes.

What we did: 
- Temporarily pinned your traffic to a healthy dedicated pool while we remediate (this reduced p99 to expected levels within ~6 minutes).
- Deployed a conservative allocator change to reduce slab fragmentation in the affected pool (rolling config with monitoring).
- Opened a follow-up engineering workstream to add proactive KV cache eviction heuristics and improve allocator telemetry.

Customer-facing M.A.P (attached): mutual_action_plan-AlpineAI.docx — contains timeline, proposed permanent fixes, and SLA remediation options.

Next actions for Alpine: please confirm whether you can tolerate a short model-variant fallback (quantized) for low-latency critical endpoints while we implement permanent fixes. We can also offer a one-time credit to offset customer impact — Marissa, Grace will coordinate on options.
